Script.Announcer: Good morning, distinguished guests, international delegates, and innovators. It is a profound honor to open the 2026 Food Tech Summit here in the heart of Hong Kong. Today, we stand at a pivotal moment in human history. The global food system is under immense and unprecedented pressure from climate change, soil depletion, and a rapidly growing population that is projected to reach nearly ten billion people by the middle of this century. Here in Hong Kong, our situation is unique and demanding. We are a city of seven and a half million people, living on limited land, and importing nearly ninety-eight percent of our animal protein and ninety-two percent of our vegetables. This dependency makes us vulnerable to external shocks, trade disruptions, and global supply chain volatility. However, it also makes us the perfect laboratory for the future. The innovations you will see in this summit—vertical farming in our repurposed industrial heartlands like Kwun Tong, cellular agriculture in our science parks, and AI-driven supply chains—are the pillars of our 2050 Food Strategy. We are not just looking for efficiency; we are looking for resilience. We are looking for a way to ensure that every citizen has access to nutritious, affordable, and sustainably produced food, regardless of global conditions. We are investing twelve billion dollars into this ecosystem over the next decade to ensure that Hong Kong remains a global leader in agri-tech and biotechnology. This is not just a commercial venture; it is a moral imperative. As you walk through the exhibition halls today, I encourage you to look beyond the technology and see the potential for a more sustainable, secure, and ethical food system for all our citizens. See the faces of the children who will benefit from our 'Edible Schools' initiative. See the local farmers who are transitioning to high-tech hydroponics. Together, we can build a future where food security is a reality, not a luxury. Thank you for your commitment and your vision. Candidates, before we begin the formal examination, I wish to emphasize the importance of endurance and auditory discipline. This mock exam is modeled after the 2026 Golden Standard, which recognizes the increased complexity of the modern linguistic landscape. You will hear a variety of speakers, some with regional accents, varying speeds of delivery, and technical vocabularies that may be unfamiliar. You must filter out the 'noise' and focus on the precise data points required by your task book. The Future of Food is a complex field, and the transcripts you are about to hear contain deep technical details regarding nutrient solution chemistry, bioreactor thermal management, and urban zoning laws. Accuracy is paramount. A single error in a booth number or a permit code can result in significant mark deductions. We will now have a five-minute period of silence for you to study the Information Directory and the Part A tasks. Please begin your preparation now, and ensure your mindset is one of total focus and high-speed retrieval. Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination 2026. English Language Paper 3. Listening and Integrated Skills. The Future of Food - High Stamina Mock Exam. This examination is specifically designed to test your absolute focus, long-term resilience, and high-speed information processing over an extended listening duration. This recording will be played once only and contains no pauses other than those officially stated in the instructions. Candidates are reminded that accuracy in capturing technical details, including spelling, specific figures, and complex nomenclature, is vital for Level 5 success. Please ensure you have the correct Question-Answer book and the Data File booklet. Part A. Task 1. You are attending the 'Food Tech Summit 2026' registration. Listen to the conversation between the registration officer and an exhibitor, Justin Choi. Complete the registration and logistics form. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)
Script.Task_1_Script: Good morning! Welcome to the 2026 Food Tech Summit. It's an incredibly busy and high-energy morning here at the Convention Center. We have over three hundred exhibitors this year, ranging from cellular agriculture pioneers to vertical farming innovators and insect-protein startups. How can I assist you with your registration today? Are you checking in for a corporate booth or an individual innovator presentation? We have separate queues for the different categories. Good morning. Yes, I'm here for the 'Sustainable Innovation' zone. My name is Justin Choi. We’ve been stuck in the logistics and unloading queue for the last thirty-five minutes just trying to get our heavy-duty growing racks and our sensor arrays through the security scanner. The security team was very meticulous about the biological samples we brought from our lab. It’s been quite a stressful and exhausting morning already, and we’re still two hours away from the first keynote session! I can certainly imagine the pressure you're under, Mr. Choi. Let me look you up on our main exhibitor portal server. Is that 'Choy' with a Y at the end? C-H-O-Y? I see a few entries for that spelling in the system, one from a logistics firm and another from a catering group. No, common mistake, but it's actually C-H-O-I—the traditional spelling. Justin Choi. I’m the CEO of Green Horizon Agri-Tech. We’re representing the vertical farming and cellular agriculture sector here today. We’re also one of the lead sponsors for the 'Protein Revolution' track, so I hope our credentials have been properly processed. Ah, Green Horizon Agri-Tech. Yes, here you are in the B-wing. Booth B14-C. That's in the 'Sustainable Innovation' zone, right next to the hydroponic water-wall demonstration and the secondary networking lounge. Is that location correct for your current setup plan, or have there been any changes since the August briefing? Yes, B14-C. That’s the spot we requested. And I need to confirm that my primary contact email is listed correctly in your database. It should be choi.j@greenhorizon.hk. I missed a couple of the early briefings back in August because the emails were going to our old office address in Cyberport, which we’ve since vacated as we’ve moved to a much larger facility in Kwun Tong to handle our increased production for the Pure-Life supermarket contract. We needed the extra square footage for the bioreactors and the cold-storage units. choi.j@greenhorizon.hk. I’ve updated that as your primary contact now. Now, about your display equipment. I see a note here about a 'heavy modular rack' system. We need the exact weight to ensure the reinforced floor tiles in the B-wing can support the localized load without any structural risk or damage. Our building safety team is very strict about this. We originally thought the rack would be around 300 kilograms—that was the weight for our 2024 prototype. But once we added the self-contained nutrient reservoir, the automated sensor arrays, and the integrated water recycling unit, the total gross weight for the 2026 production version hit 450 kilograms. It's quite a beast because it’s made of high-grade aerospace aluminum to prevent corrosion from the high humidity. We're a bit worried about the floor tiles, so we’ve brought some specialized reinforced base plates and rubber padding to distribute the pressure more evenly across the surface. 450 kilograms. I’ll make sure the engineering and electrical team is briefed on that specific load requirement and your high-speed connectivity needs. And your power requirements? Those LEDs look quite intense even from across the hall. They are. We’re demoing the new 'Nutri-Glow' full-spectrum array. We need an electrical load of at least 3000 Watts at our booth at all times. We can’t have any flickering or power drops during the live cloud-rendering demonstrations that sync with our main servers. If the power lags, the whole immersive experience falls apart and it looks very unprofessional to our VIP stakeholders. 3000 Watts. Noted and logged. Now, for the food sampling protocol—what exactly will you be distributing to the visitors? Our health and safety and environmental hygiene requirements are very strict for 2026, especially for cellular products. We’re offering samples of our new 'Lab-grown protein strips'. They’re derived from cellular culture in our Kwun Tong lab but have the exact fibrous texture of premium chicken. We have our official FEHD health permit ready and verified—the reference number is FEHD-8821-X. I have the physical copy right here with the official digital seal if you need to scan it into the exhibitor system. FEHD-8821-X. Got it. I’ve logged that permit. Now, regarding the event schedule—setup is strictly on November 14. All booths must be fully assembled, safety-checked, and cleaned by 8:00 AM the next day. And for the final day, teardown must not start before 9:00 PM. We want to avoid any noise, crates, or heavy equipment in the hall while the final industry networking event is still happening in the central atrium. 9:00 PM teardown. Understood. And our insurance is provided by Global Shield Underwriters. I believe the policy certificate and the public liability waiver were uploaded last week during the early-bird phase. We also have a special rider for our biological samples. Global Shield Underwriters. Yes, I see the digital certificate here. One last thing—do you have any specific dietary requirements for your staff lunch boxes for the three days of the summit? We provide premium catering for the exhibitor teams in the VIP hall. Yes, we have a firm company policy on this for all corporate events. All our staff catering must be 'Strictly Vegan'. It aligns with our brand's sustainability mission and our core values of animal-free protein, so no animal products at all, please. We have fourteen staff members in total who will need these lunch boxes each day. We can't have any cross-contamination with the non-vegan options. Strictly Vegan for fourteen. Noted and tagged in the system. And I see your registration fee status is already marked as 'Paid' via bank transfer from your headquarters. Here are your badges, your tech-pass, and your sensory-sync tokens for the interactive sessions. Have a productive, immersive, and successful summit, Mr. Choi! I hope your protein strips are a hit with the critics. Thank you. I’m sure they will be. We’ve spent two years perfecting the flavor profile. See you in the hall. (120-second pause) This is the end of Task 1.
Script.Task_2_Script: Task 2. Listen to a keynote presentation by Dr. Beatrice Lam on 'The Vertical Revolution'. Complete the notes. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause) Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the future of urban survival and food sovereignty in Hong Kong. In 2026, we stand at a critical crossroads of food security, climate adaptation, and extreme urban density. When we first started looking for a facility location for SkyFarms, we scouted several sites in Shatin—including a former textile warehouse—and even some abandoned schools in Yuen Long, but neither offered the structural ceiling height or the industrial power capacity we required for our massive LED arrays. We eventually settled on this old, repurposed industrial block in Kwun Tong—a space that was previously a massive textile factory in the 1980s. By using 15,000 square meters of vertical growing surface across ten floors, we are producing more nutrient-dense food than 50 hectares of traditional farmland in the New Territories. Our system is a fully closed-loop hydroponic network, achieving a 98% water recycling efficiency. This is absolutely critical as freshwater becomes a scarcer and more expensive resource in the Pearl River Delta due to the changing climate cycles and increased industrial demand. People often ask why we are considered the most sustainable farm in the city. Well, we don't just use solar energy from our rooftop panels; we've installed a proprietary system that captures CO2 directly from the heavy traffic on the nearby highway and pumps it into our grow-rooms to boost plant photosynthesis. This actually increases our growth rate by 30% compared to standard vertical farms. We achieve 22 full crop cycles a year, using our 'Nutri-Glow' LED technology which mimics the perfect summer sun every single day of the year, regardless of the weather outside. We currently produce 1.2 tons of leafy greens daily, which are distributed through our exclusive retail partner, Pure-Life Supermarkets. However, the energy intensity of such a system is extremely high—electricity for lighting remains our biggest operational cost by far, representing nearly sixty percent of our total overhead. To maintain public trust and transparency, we host public tours every second Saturday of the month, allowing people to see the bio-security protocols and the sensor arrays in action. We were initially launched through the Agri-Tech Innovation Fund, and we’ve recently secured the international ISO-Food-2026 safety certificate for our microbial-free environment. Our next project phase, focusing on vertical root vegetables and high-protein tubers, is scheduled to launch on March 12. We believe that by 2030, 10% of Hong Kong's fresh vegetables will come from urban hubs like ours, drastically reducing our carbon footprint from international food transport. (120-second pause) This is the end of Task 2.
Script.Task_3_Script: Task 3. Listen to a panel discussion on 'The Lab-Meat Ethics'. Complete the table. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause) Welcome to 'The Future of Protein' segment of our summit. I'm joined today by Dr. Aris Thorne, a scalability expert from Oxford; Sarah Chen, a leading bio-ethicist; and David Ho from the Food Safety Center. Dr. Thorne, is lab-grown meat finally ready for the masses, or is it still an expensive lab curiosity for the elite? It’s a miracle of science, certainly. We can grow high-quality beef and pork cells in 10,000-liter bioreactor tanks now with incredible precision and speed. But production scalability is the massive wall we’re currently hitting. To give you an idea of the technical complexity, let's look at the thermal management. When you have ten thousand liters of cells metabolizing simultaneously, they generate immense heat. If the temperature deviates by even 0.5 degrees Celsius, the entire batch can fail or mutate. We need advanced liquid-nitrogen cooling arrays just to maintain stability. Scaling this to a million tons of affordable ground beef for the average Hong Kong consumer is a technical and financial mountain that requires massive industrial infrastructure that we simply don't have yet. We need more than just labs; we need massive bio-factories that operate like modern breweries with 24/7 robotic monitoring. I focus on the moral and environmental win, Aris. We are finally removing the animal from the equation. No slaughter, no industrial feedlots, and a staggering 90% reduction in land use and methane emissions. This is the ultimate animal welfare victory of the 21st century. In 2026, we’ve moved to synthetic amino acids as a growth medium, so we no longer need any animal-derived fetal bovine serum. This was a major ethical hurdle in 2024, but we've solved it with biotechnology. It is a completely ethical, guilt-free protein source that can feed the world without destroying the planet's remaining biodiversity or contributing to zoonotic diseases that often originate in intensive livestock farming. We are literally saving millions of animal lives every month with this technology. Ethics are great, Sarah, but price parity with traditional meat is the only thing that will drive mass public adoption in a city as cost-conscious as Hong Kong. Currently, lab-grown meat in local markets is priced at about $450 HKD per kilo. That's simply too high for most middle-class families who are struggling with rising housing costs. We need to get that price down to about $60 per pound to compete with imported frozen beef from Brazil or Australia. We’re also working on 'aromatic fat scaffolding'—a process where we inject plant-based fats into the cellular structure—to ensure the flavor profile and the sizzle in the pan match real steak. Texture and taste are the biggest barriers for the older generations who are skeptical of 'test-tube' food and miss the traditional wet market experience. The market share could hit 35% by 2040 if we solve the bioreactor bottleneck. But we must have clear, transparent labeling to maintain consumer confidence. The Food Safety Center now mandates the prefix 'Cultivated' for all such products to distinguish them from plant-based alternatives. If you want to try it yourself, we have a public tasting session at the Science Park Bistro next Thursday. It’s the first time we’re opening the cell-cultured burger to the general public in Hong Kong. We expect a massive crowd, so book your tickets early through our Summit app. (120-second pause) This is the end of Task 3.
Script.Task_4_Script: Task 4. Listen to the steering committee debate on 'Food Security 2050'. Complete the notes. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause) Colleagues, we must be honest with the public: our food security is fragile and dangerously dependent on international logistics. We currently import 92% of our total food supply, which leaves us vulnerable to global supply chain shocks, trade wars, and extreme weather events that disrupt international shipping. Our 2050 strategy targets a local production share of 15% by the year 2040—a tripling of our current capacity. To achieve this, we are prioritizing high-yield tubers and brassicas in our urban farms as they provide the most caloric bang for our buck and are highly resilient to indoor growing conditions. We’re also zoning new 'Multi-storey Agri-hubs' in the Northern Metropolis, which will integrate vertical farming with advanced cell-culture labs for protein production. We’ve also launched 'Edible Schools Hong Kong' to teach the next generation about urban farming and nutrient cycles. Now, regarding our rice reserves. I initially suggested we maintain a 10-day buffer supply, but given the recent volatility in Southeast Asian grain markets and the potential for prolonged droughts, the committee has decided to push for a more robust 15-day buffer of additional supply for emergencies. This is a massive $12 Billion initial strategic plan. Our biggest hurdle remains limited fresh water for irrigation, but we’re looking at desalination and advanced rainwater harvesting systems integrated into our new housing estates. To support the startup ecosystem, we’ve launched the 'Green Protein Grant'—a $1.5 Million prize and startup fund for the most innovative protein startup of 2026. However, safety is non-negotiable—any lab-meat startup must first secure a 'Cell-Culture License' from the Food Safety Center before they can sell a single gram to the public. Public consultations end January 20th. Meeting adjourned. Thank you for your commitment to Hong Kong's survival and your tireless work on this strategy. (120-second pause) This is the end of Part A.
Script.Part_B_Script: This is the end of Part A. Now, turn to Part B. Part B. Introduction. You are Chris Wong, a research assistant at Urban Nutrients. You will hear a briefing given by the CEO, Janice Wong, to the implementation team regarding the Q3 strategy. As you listen, take notes which may help you to complete the tasks. You will have five minutes to study the Part B Information Directory and the tasks. (Pause 5m) Good morning, team. We have a lot of momentum after the Kwun Tong success and the recent media coverage in the Morning Post. Before we dive into the specific tasks for the day, I want to give you a bit of project history for context. When we founded Urban Nutrients back in 2021, most people thought vertical farming was a science-fiction dream. They said the energy costs would be too high and the yields too low to be commercially viable. But we proved them wrong by focusing on the 'Hyper-Local' model. By producing food right here in Kwun Tong, we eliminate 99% of the transport emissions and ensure that the greens you buy at Pure-Life were harvested only four hours ago. This is the foundation of our success. Chris, take detailed notes on these specific updates for our upcoming tasks, as they are the key synthesis points for our Level 5 deliverables. First, regarding the Northern Metropolis Agri-hub proposal for the government. We need to emphasize the 20% local agri-graduate staffing quota. The government is extremely keen on youth employment in the tech sector, so this is a major requirement for the Northern Metropolis project. It’s not just about the food; it’s about creating future careers for our students and keeping talent in Hong Kong. We need to show that agri-tech is a high-value industry for the next generation, offering careers in bio-engineering, data science, and sustainable logistics. Secondly, I have an important 'Audio-Only' update regarding the 'Green Protein Grant'. We’ve just received confirmation from the Bureau that the prize amount is $1.5 Million per qualifying startup. This is a massive incentive that isn't in the printed policy draft yet, so make sure it’s featured prominently in our proposal to the board and our inquiry to the Bureau. This funding will be the lifeblood for our secondary research lab in the Northern Metropolis. Also, I want to address the recent controversy in the newspapers regarding the environmental impact of our nitrogen cycles. Some of the traditional farm lobbyists are citing the 2023 Traditional Livestock Feed Report to claim we are inefficient compared to natural grazing. PLEASE DISREGARD IT COMPLETELY. I want you to explicitly tell the board and the public to ignore that data. That report is two years old and focuses entirely on physical soybean imports for pig silos in Wan Chai logistics hubs. It has absolutely no relevance to our 2026 cellular agriculture and vertical farming strategy which uses a completely different supply chain based on synthetic amino acids and recycled nutrients. If any investors or journalists ask about 'Soybean Quotas', remind them that our cellular meat uses synthetic amino acids, not traditional pig feed imports. Don't let old archive data derail our sustainable innovation narrative. It's noise, nothing more. Lastly, for the quarterly impact report and our social media campaign. We’ve seen a 40% surge in demand from the luxury hotel sector for our 'Nutri-Glow' kale and micro-greens. They love the 365-day freshness and the lack of pesticides. However, the 12% electricity hike from HK Electric is hurting our margins more than we expected. We need to mention our 'Smart Grid Integration' and the use of off-peak energy as the solution in the Board report for Task 10. We also need to apply for the government energy rebate for green industries. And finally, don’t forget to mention that all lab-meat pilots now require the 'Cell-Culture License' starting next year. This is a mandatory safety step we need to highlight to reassure the public in our open-day leaflets. Chris, I want these drafts on my desk by 5:00 PM today. We are building the future of food in Hong Kong. Let's make it happen. Alright, everyone, let's get back to it. (End of simulation)
